BATTLE OF THE MARSHALL ISLANDS

USA vs Japan · 2 Player Strategy

Tutorial

Pick something to learn (lessons use Map 1: Marshall Islands)

Skirmish Lab

Pick the units for each side, then fight in the real battle screen. Planes fill carriers first (6 per carrier); extra planes fly in on their own. Nothing here affects a real game.

Rules Book

Goal & victory
  • Win by reaching 2000 VP, checked at the end of a full round (after both players have had a turn).
  • Or win instantly by destroying every enemy military unit on the board (units waiting in the production area don’t count; cargo aboard transports does).
  • If both players reach 2000 VP in the same round, sudden death begins: only total annihilation wins.
  • Capturing the enemy base gives a one-time 150 VP bonus.
Turn order
  1. Collect income
  2. Purchase units
  3. Movement
  4. Combat
  5. Capture / ownership resolution
  6. Pass the turn

Purchased units wait in your production area and can’t act until your next turn. A coin flip decides who goes first.

Starting setup
  • Each side starts with 0 gold and 0 VP and owns only its own base.
  • All islands, sea zones and currency islands start unowned and must be captured.
  • Starting force (13 units): 2 fighters, 1 cruiser, 3 destroyers, 2 transports, 1 tank, 4 soldiers.
  • Where each side starts depends on the map you pick (see Maps). Starting units begin in or beside your base.
Maps

You choose one of five maps after setting up the match. Every map is 18 x 13 squares and has the same objectives: 4 major islands (12 VP), 6 currency islands (10 gold) and 3 sea zones (8 VP). Only the layout and the base positions change. Your starting units and every new purchase appear in your own base.

  • Income is collected at the start of your turn. Newly captured land pays from your next turn.
  • Captured territory stays yours even if you leave it. An eligible enemy unit entering an empty one takes it.
  • Carriers, transports and aircraft cannot capture territory.

Maximum 109 units per side. Gold can be saved with no limit. Some HP values are test values and may change.

Movement
  • Move horizontally, vertically or diagonally; every square costs 1 movement point.
  • Stack any number of friendly units; split and merge freely.
  • Moving into an enemy-occupied square starts combat; you can’t pass through enemies.
  • Units that fought have used their movement for the turn.
Combat
  • Every unit has its own HP. Damage carries over between identical units.
  • Damage is rolled with 2d6 using a table for each attacker type.
  • Fighters fight fighters. Bombers only support ground attacks.
  • Ships target battleships, then cruisers, then destroyers. Carriers and transports are hit last. Ground units target tanks, then soldiers.
  • Carriers and transports do not attack.
  • Retreat may be attempted before the first attack and after each full combat round.
  • Surrounded: a unit with no safe square to retreat to can't retreat. If you try anyway, it is locked: it can't attack or retreat for the rest of that turn (the lock ends when the next turn starts).
Aircraft
  • Fighter range 5, bomber range 8 squares, counted for the whole trip from launch to landing, not each way. Diagonals cost 1.
  • Carriers (max 3 per side) hold up to 6 planes in any mix of fighters, torpedo bombers and dive bombers. If the carrier moves toward the target add +1 range, away −1.
  • Aircraft land at your base, friendly land you control, or a carrier (fighters, torpedo and dive bombers; 6 planes per carrier; heavy bombers never), but not on currency islands. A plane with no legal landing spot gets one turn of warning: it regains its full range next turn to find a place to land, and is lost only if it still can't land.
  • Planes in the same square as your carrier move with it for free (up to 6 per carrier). To keep a plane behind, move that plane first.
Planes in battle
  • Fighter (10 gold, HP 1): attacks aircraft only. Torpedo bomber (20 gold, HP 2): attacks ships only, battleship damage. Dive bomber (20 gold, HP 2): attacks ships and ground, cruiser damage. Heavy bomber (USA B-17 Flying Fortress / Japan G4M Betty; 20 gold, HP 4): attacks ships and ground, lands only at a base or island.
  • Before each combat round, pick which planes each carrier launches. Planes kept aboard are safe; launched planes return to the carrier at the end of the round.
  • Torpedo and dive bombers attack once, then have a 3-round cooldown. A Skip button saves them for later with no cooldown.
  • Heavy bombers (B-17 / Betty) can't land on carriers. They join as separate units, attack once, then leave at the end of the turn.
  • If a carrier is destroyed, all planes aboard are lost. Destroyed planes go to the destroyed list. Cooldowns reset when combat ends.

  • Cooldowns count combat rounds. AA fire: battleships, cruisers and destroyers may shoot at aircraft instead of a ship in the naval phase (destroyers and cruisers use the destroyer table, battleships the cruiser table).
  • Tank and soldier abilities have a 2-round cooldown; ½ damage rounds up.
  • These rules are active in the main game. When units from both sides share a square, the battle screen opens with everything in that square, and the survivors return to the board afterward.
AI difficulty
  • Easy: simple opponent that makes mistakes. Retreating units heal fully (agreed test rule).
  • Normal: sensible buying, uses planes, avoids clearly losing fights, sometimes hesitates.
  • Hard: plans invasions with escorts and bombardment, guards its base, counters your army.
  • Nightmare: the strongest tactical AI: weighs odds and threats every move, concentrates force, picks targets and abilities carefully. It gets no income or damage bonuses.
  • Retreating units only heal fully on Easy.
Battle backgrounds
  • The battle screen changes with the battlefield: open sea for naval fights, sky and clouds when only aircraft fight, a beach for amphibious landings, and jungle for fighting on land.
Shore bombardment
  • When you unload troops onto an island or base held by enemy ground units, you may first bombard with battleships that are in a sea square next to the target.
  • Each battleship fires once (battleship damage table) at the defenders, tanks first. A battleship that fought a battle this turn, or already bombarded, can't fire.
  • Bombardment only happens as part of a real landing, can't capture anything alone, and is optional: choose No bombardment to land without it.
  • Heavy bombers and dive bombers that fly to a defended island attack the ground units in the air phase of that battle.
Transports & invasions
  • A transport carries 3 soldiers or 2 tanks, never mixed.
  • Load and unload only when adjacent to a friendly base or an island. Each costs the unit 1 movement point.
  • Landing on an empty island or enemy base is uncontested. If enemies are there, combat starts.
  • If a transport is destroyed, its cargo is lost.
Bases
  • To capture an enemy base you need 2 soldiers and 1 tank there.
  • While your base is occupied you get no income and can’t produce units, but your saved gold and VP are kept.
  • Retaking your base restores it, and income and production resume on your next turn.
